title: Descent of an enriched Quillen adjunction without stability
statement:
Use unbounded cochain complexes and quasi-isomorphisms of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived chain enrichment and enriched localization of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. Work in universes containing all categories below. Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be complete and cocomplete locally presentable categories enriched, tensored and cotensored over $\operatorname{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$. In each category assume retract-closed classes $C,F,W$, with $W$ satisfying two-out-of-three, and functorial weak factorization systems $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ generated by sets. A weak factorization system means factorization of every map and mutually characterized diagonal-lifting classes; locally presentable means generated under filtered colimits for some regular cardinal by a small set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve those colimits. Assume the enriched model axiom: for $i:A\to B$ in $C$ and $p:X\to Y$ in $F$, the induced map $H(B,X)\to H(A,X)\times_{H(A,Y)}H(B,Y)$ is degreewise surjective, and is a quasi-isomorphism if $i$ or $p$ lies in $W$. Here $H$ denotes the enriched Hom complex. An object is cofibrant if its initial map lies in $C$, and fibrant if its terminal map lies in $F$. Write $\mathcal A_c,\mathcal B_f$ for the full enriched subcategories of such objects. Use the derived mapping-object convention of [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison].

Let $L:\mathcal A\rightleftarrows\mathcal B:R$ be an enriched adjunction, meaning a natural isomorphism of complexes $H_{\mathcal B}(LX,Y)\cong H_{\mathcal A}(X,RY)$ compatible with the enriched actions. Suppose $L$ preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, where trivial means also in $W$. Then restriction of $L$ to $\mathcal A_c$ and of $R$ to $\mathcal B_f$, followed by enriched localization and inverses of the localized inclusion equivalences, defines enhanced functors $\mathbb L L,\mathbb R R$ and an equivalence
$$R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal B[W^{-1}]}(\mathbb L L X,Y)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A[W^{-1}]}(X,\mathbb R R Y).$$
Its restriction to $\mathcal A_c^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B_f$ is the given enriched adjunction isomorphism, and it is coherent and natural in both variables. The extension with its specified restriction is unique up to a contractible space of choices. More generally, this descent retains all naturality in any finite number of relative enriched parameter categories whenever the restricted functors and adjunction isomorphisms are enriched and homotopical separately in these parameters (homotopical means carrying their specified weak equivalences to equivalences). No stability assumption or enriched replacement functor is required.

source.place: Agent-formulated model foundation for paragraph 2: enriched adjunction descent. No Stacks tag is asserted for this chain-enriched statement.

proof.text: First check the right Quillen properties directly. A lifting square from a map $i$ of $\mathcal A$ to $Rp$, for a map $p$ of $\mathcal B$, corresponds under the underlying adjunction to a lifting square from $Li$ to $p$; the same adjunction identifies its fillers. If $p$ is a fibration, every trivial cofibration $i$ has $Li$ a trivial cofibration, so the square has a filler. The weak factorization system $(C\cap W,F)$ makes $Rp$ a fibration. If $p$ is a trivial fibration, use all cofibrations $i$ and $(C,F\cap W)$ instead to show that $Rp$ is a trivial fibration. Also $L0_{\mathcal A}$ is initial, since maps from it to any $Y$ correspond to the unique map $0_{\mathcal A}\to RY$; dually $R*_{\mathcal B}$ is terminal. Preservation of cofibrations by $L$, applied to initial maps, and preservation of fibrations by $R$, applied to terminal maps, therefore give $L(\mathcal A_c)\subseteq\mathcal B_c$ and $R(\mathcal B_f)\subseteq\mathcal A_f$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, middle derived mapping-complex comparison; agent-supplied foundation: adjoint lifting squares and preservation of the required objects

proof.text: Let $u:X\to X'$ be a weak equivalence between cofibrant objects of $\mathcal A$. Apply [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] to obtain $u=pi$, with $p:Z\to X'$ a trivial fibration, $i:X\to Z$ a cofibration, and a cofibration $s:X'\to Z$ satisfying $ps=1$. Two-out-of-three, applied to $pi=u$ and $ps=1$, makes $i$ and $s$ weak equivalences. Hence $Li$ and $Ls$ are trivial cofibrations, in particular weak equivalences. Since $(Lp)(Ls)=1$, two-out-of-three makes $Lp$ a weak equivalence as well, and then $Lu=(Lp)(Li)$ is one. Thus the enriched restriction $L_c:\mathcal A_c\to\mathcal B_c$ preserves the inherited weak equivalences.

source.place: Paragraph 2, middle derived mapping-complex comparison; agent-supplied foundation: Brown argument on the cofibrant domain

proof.text: Let $v:Y\to Y'$ be a weak equivalence between fibrant objects of $\mathcal B$. The dual assertion of [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] gives $v=pi$, where $i:Y\to Z$ is a trivial cofibration, $p:Z\to Y'$ is a fibration, and a fibration $r:Z\to Y$ satisfies $ri=1$. Two-out-of-three makes $p$ and $r$ trivial fibrations. Step 1 makes $Rp$ and $Rr$ weak equivalences. From $(Rr)(Ri)=1$ it follows that $Ri$ is a weak equivalence, and hence $Rv=(Rp)(Ri)$ is one. Thus the enriched restriction $R_f:\mathcal B_f\to\mathcal A_f$ preserves the inherited weak equivalences.

source.place: Paragraph 2, middle derived mapping-complex comparison; agent-supplied foundation: Brown argument on the fibrant domain

proof.text:
Write $q_{\mathcal A},q_{\mathcal B}$ for the enriched localization functors. By [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal], Steps 2 and 3 induce enriched functors $\overline L:\mathcal A_c[W^{-1}]\to\mathcal B_c[W^{-1}]$ and $\overline R:\mathcal B_f[W^{-1}]\to\mathcal A_f[W^{-1}]$. Apply [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison] in both model categories: the localized inclusions $j_{\mathcal A,c},j_{\mathcal A,f},j_{\mathcal B,c},j_{\mathcal B,f}$ are equivalences. Consequently the composites
$$\mathbb L L=j_{\mathcal B,c}\,\overline L\,j_{\mathcal A,c}^{-1},\qquad \mathbb R R=j_{\mathcal A,f}\,\overline R\,j_{\mathcal B,f}^{-1}$$
are the desired enhanced functors. The localization universal property supplies their specified comparisons with $q_{\mathcal B}L$ on $\mathcal A_c$ and $q_{\mathcal A}R$ on $\mathcal B_f$. All hypotheses of the mapping-comparison node are precisely the completeness, presentability, two lifting systems and enriched model axiom assumed here.

source.place: Paragraph 2, middle derived mapping-complex comparison; agent-supplied foundation: construct the functors by localization and inclusion equivalences

proof.text: For $X\in\mathcal A_c$ and $Y\in\mathcal B_f$, Step 1 makes $LX$ cofibrant and $RY$ fibrant. The mixed-domain mapping comparison of [lem-coef-dg-model-mapping-comparison] therefore identifies the two restricted derived mapping bifunctors with $H_{\mathcal B}(LX,Y)$ and $H_{\mathcal A}(X,RY)$, respectively, interpreted in $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$. These identifications are enriched and natural as bifunctors, rather than just identifications of individual Hom sets. The assumed enriched adjunction gives an isomorphism between these complexes, natural and compatible with the enriched actions. Each bifunctor carries a weak equivalence in either variable to a quasi-isomorphism: use Steps 2 and 3 for $L$ and $R$, and the mixed-domain weak-equivalence invariance in the cited comparison node for the Hom complexes. Thus the given adjunction is an equivalence between two relative enriched bifunctors on $\mathcal A_c^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B_f$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, middle derived mapping-complex comparison; agent-supplied foundation: identify the restricted comparison and verify its relative hypotheses

proof.text: Apply the multivariable assertion of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] to the bifunctors and their transformation in Step 5. It applies to the opposite in the first variable. Restriction along the two localization maps is an equivalence of enhanced functor categories, fully faithful on transformations and every higher homotopy; it therefore extends the specified adjunction isomorphism. Next invert the localized inclusion equivalences from Step 4, using the same universal property's assertion about such inverses. The result is the displayed equivalence of derived mapping objects on $\mathcal A[W^{-1}]^{\mathrm{op}}\times\mathcal B[W^{-1}]$. Its components are equivalences by the cited pointwise criterion. Its specified restriction is exactly Step 5's original enriched adjunction under the mapping comparisons, since the extension was taken over that transformation, including its restriction. Full faithfulness supplies naturality and all coherences, and the contractible extension-space assertion supplies uniqueness with the specified restriction. No replacement functor was chosen; stability was not used.

source.place: Paragraph 2, middle derived mapping-complex comparison; agent-supplied foundation: descend the specified comparison, its coherences, and its uniqueness

proof.text: Finally, include any given finite list of relative enriched parameter categories as additional variables throughout Steps 4-6. By hypothesis the restricted functors and adjunction transformations are enriched in these variables and preserve their specified weak equivalences separately. They therefore satisfy exactly the additional-variable hypotheses of [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal]. Its multivariable restriction equivalence, compatible with substitution, composition, and coherent diagrams, extends this entire specified diagram at once. This gives the claimed parameter naturality, including its higher coherences; the fiber over the specified restricted diagram is again contractible by that node. Applying this to the empty list recovers Step 6, so no additional condition on parameters or their model structures has entered the argument.
